where: Section 1, paragraph on the shift register
problem: "After eight pulses, the two bytes have swapped places. A 16-bit transfer simply repeats this 16 times." It is unclear what "this" repeats. A student can read it as repeating the 8-bit exchange 16 times, which gives 128 bits, not 16.
fix: "After eight pulses, the two bytes have swapped places, so a 16-bit transfer needs 16 SCLK pulses: the 8-bit exchange is performed twice."

problem: "its MISO goes to the next slave" does not say which pin of the next slave receives the data. Read literally, MISO goes to MISO, which would be wrong.
fix: "the master MOSI goes to the first slave's data input, that slave's MISO goes to the next slave's MOSI (data input), and the last slave's MISO returns to the master MISO."

problem: The answer does not state the practical limit: a daisy chain works only if every device has a pass-through shift register (or the chain is built for it), and each device receives all bits shifted through it, so a transfer is four bytes long for four sensors.
fix: Add: "A daisy chain needs slaves that support pass-through shifting, and every transfer shifts all bits through every device, so reading one sensor means shifting 4 bytes; many sensors do not offer this."
